claim: The two new AppError ids model.command_response.is_valid.response_type.app_error and model.command_response.is_valid.text.app_error do not exist in server/i18n/en.json, so NewAppError's eager Translate returns the raw key string as the Message that reaches API clients and logs; the Makefile i18n-check target does not run mmgotool i18n check so CI will not catch it.
raw: 1. The two new i18n keys do not exist in `server/i18n/en.json`, so the error message is the raw key string.

claim: The new text-length check is a newly invented limit on a public integration contract: previously any body up to MaxIntegrationResponseSize (1MB) was accepted and ephemeral/blank-default responses go through SendEphemeralPost with no length validation, so third-party slash commands returning large ephemeral text that work today will now fail the whole command with an HTTP 500, with no release note, docs update, or config gate.
raw: 2. The text-length check is a newly-invented limit that breaks ephemeral integration responses that work today.

claim: The 65535 limit is a bare literal that silently duplicates model.PostMessageMaxBytesV2 and is byte-based, whereas the limit actually enforced on the resulting post is GetMaxPostSize()/PostMessageMaxRunesV2 = 16383 runes; so 20000 ASCII chars in_channel pass the model check and fail downstream while ~21.8k CJK runes are rejected — the check should be utf8.RuneCountInString against the post rune limit, which is a config value the model package cannot see, suggesting it belongs at the app layer.
raw: 3. The 65535 limit is byte-based, hardcoded, and doesn't correspond to any limit the product actually enforces.

claim: Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam decode via CommandResponseFromJSON and so inherit the new strictness, but plugin and built-in command responses never pass through IsValid on the way out (tryExecutePluginCommand/tryExecuteBuiltInCommand return structs directly to HandleCommandResponse); a plugin returning response_type "foo" or over-cap text is serialized by the server and rejected by every Client4 with nil, err, losing the payload; also a forward-compat hazard if a new response_type is ever added — restrict validation to inbound-integration paths and keep the client decoder permissive.
raw: 4. Validation is enforced on the consumer (`Client4`) but not on the producer, so the Go client can reject its own server's legitimate output.

claim: Calling IsValid() from inside CommandResponseFromJSON deviates from the package convention: the analogous IncomingWebhookRequestFromJSON decodes and normalizes but does not validate, and across model IsValid() is called by the app/store layer at a trust boundary it chooses (e.g. Post.IsValid(maxPostSize)); folding validation into the decoder makes the policy non-optional for every consumer of the public module. Add IsValid as a method but do not call it from the decoder.
raw: 5. Validation in the decoder deviates from the package convention.

claim: The text/plain branch (CommandResponseFromPlainText) is untouched, so a 900KB text/plain body is accepted while byte-identical application/json content is rejected — the limit is trivially bypassable via the Content-Type header; both branches of CommandResponseFromHTTPBody should agree.
raw: 6. The plain-text branch bypasses all of it, so "strict validation" is only half-applied.

claim: IsValid's `if resp == nil { continue }` lets {"extra_responses":[null]} pass and yield []*CommandResponse{nil}; downstream HandleCommandResponse iterates ExtraResponses and HandleCommandResponsePost dereferences response.Type/response.Props — a reachable nil-pointer panic from commandWebhook and any custom slash command response, with no recover() in the web/api4 handler chain. Reject or filter nil entries instead. Also IsValid recurses arbitrarily deep, the app processes one level, and attachment normalization is one level deep — three different depths for the same structure.
raw: 7. The new validation walks past a reachable nil-pointer panic instead of closing it.
